content:
incident-bot: Pager: high error rate (5xx) on /v1/generate — prod-canary — 60s spike, 45% errors :rotating_light:

sanjay: acked. I'm on it. paging oncall.

maya: looking at logs now, opening the canary stream.

carla: any deploys around that time?

ops-runner: yes, just rolled out canary v2.1.0 to 10% at 11:03 UTC — rollout job: deploy/canary/v2.1.0 (id: deploy-8932)

leo: stacktraces show repeated KMS decrypt failures: "AccessDeniedException: user is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:...:key/1234-rotated"

maya: that looks bad — new image expects new KMS key (ROTATED_KEY_ARN) to be available to service role.

sanjay: hold traffic to canary. Can someone flip feature flag or kill-switch?

carla: doing feature flag kill now: POST /flags/traffic-split -d '{"canary_v2":0}' -> using admin token (masked)

incident-bot: Feature flag update queued by carla — canary_v2 -> 0% :white_check_mark:

ops-runner: traffic pulled off canary, errors drop to baseline. Good. But rollout rollback failed when trying to redeploy previous image due to missing ENV var in the deployment job: KMS_KEY_OVERRIDE not set in cluster config.

maya: root cause: during key rotation earlier today ops rotated key and updated deployment manifest to reference ROTATED_KEY_ARN. The rotation step didn't include granting decrypt permission to the inference-service role. The new key's key policy lacks the service principal.

leo: reproducer logs:
```
[2026-03-15T11:04:12Z] inference: failed to init keystore: kms.Decrypt error AccessDeniedException
[2026-03-15T11:04:12Z] inference: falling back to null keystore -> requests 503
```

carla: mitigation options:
- add decrypt permission to rotated key policy
- patch deployment env to point at previous key (OLD_KEY_ARN) temporarily
- finish rollback after fixing job env var

sanjay: prioritize fastest safe: patch key policy to allow role decrypt, and keep canary at 0% until validated. Who can apply the key policy?

ops-runner: I can. Applying key policy change now:
```
aws kms put-key-policy --key-id 1234-rotated --policy file://allow-inference-role.json
```
policy snippet used: "{
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/inference-service-role"},
    "Action": "kms:Decrypt"
  }]
}"

incident-bot: Audit: kms policy change by ops-runner recorded (id: audit-8472).

support-bot: customer-impact: ~12% of requests in the affected window returned 5xx. Top callers: api-key:prod-customer-42, prod-customer-7. Logged for CS follow-up.

maya: post-change, decrypt errors stopped and canary services started healthy checks passing in ~30s.

carla: will slowly reintroduce canary to 5% and monitor.

ops-runner: added a temporary env override to deployment too so rollback path works: set KMS_KEY_OVERRIDE=OLD_KEY_ARN in canary deployment job config.

sanjay: good. please create an incident ticket with timeline + affected customers + remediation. I'll do a 5min handoff to next oncall then mark incident mitigated.

oncall-next: I'm up for the handoff, thanks. Key action items for postmortem: 
- ensure KMS rotation runbook includes IAM grants (add checklist)
- fail deployment if referenced KMS key policy doesn't allow service role decrypt
- add alert for sudden spike in kms.Decrypt AccessDenied exceptions

carla: filing postmortem: https://phabricator.redwood/INC-8721 (draft)

incident-bot: Incident mitigated — status: resolved (temporary fix). Created incident record INC-8721.

sanjay: closing oncall for now. follow-up owners: ops-runner (policy change), devexp (deployment guard), maya (monitoring).

leo: thumbs up. we should also rotate back to OLD_KEY after clean rotation and test with a canary that has added policy.

support-bot: CS notified, email templates queued for affected customers.

carla: final note: no data exposure, just decryption failures. Will add blameless postmortem tomorrow. :pencil2:
